plan.title: School Enrolment & Infrastructure Dashboard
plan.subtitle: Tracking enrolment trends, gender balance, and facility gaps across schools

panels.title: Total Schools
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "School Code") AS n FROM "school_enrolment_by_year"

panels.title: Schools with Functional Girls' Toilets
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM "school_infrastructure" WHERE "Toilets functional (girls)" = 'Yes'

panels.title: Enrolment Trend by Gender
panels.sql: SELECT '2022' AS year, SUM("Girls 2022") AS girls, SUM("Boys 2022") AS boys FROM "school_enrolment_by_year" UNION ALL SELECT '2023', SUM("Girls 2023"), SUM("Boys 2023") FROM "school_enrolment_by_year" UNION ALL SELECT '2024', SUM("Girls 2024"), SUM("Boys 2024") FROM "school_enrolment_by_year" ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Girls vs Boys Enrolment (2024)
panels.sql: SELECT 'Girls' AS gender, SUM("Girls 2024") AS count FROM "school_enrolment_by_year" UNION ALL SELECT 'Boys', SUM("Boys 2024") FROM "school_enrolment_by_year"

panels.title: Infrastructure Gaps
panels.sql: SELECT 'No Girls Toilets' AS gap, COUNT(*) AS count FROM "school_infrastructure" WHERE "Toilets functional (girls)" = 'No' UNION ALL SELECT 'No Drinking Water', COUNT(*) FROM "school_infrastructure" WHERE "Drinking water" = 'No' UNION ALL SELECT 'No Electricity', COUNT(*) FROM "school_infrastructure" WHERE "Electricity" = 'No'

panels.title: Schools with Multiple Infrastructure Gaps
panels.sql: SELECT "School Code", "Toilets functional (girls)" AS toilets, "Drinking water" AS water, "Electricity" AS electricity FROM "school_infrastructure" WHERE ("Toilets functional (girls)" = 'No' OR "Drinking water" = 'No' OR "Electricity" = 'No') ORDER BY "School Code" LIMIT 10

plan.narrative:
The dashboard covers {{p1}} schools with a total 2024 enrolment of {{p2}} students. 

Enrolment trends show a steady increase from 2022 to 2024 for both genders, with girls' enrolment reaching {{p4[2].girls}} and boys' enrolment reaching {{p4[2].boys}} in 2024. 

In 2024, girls account for {{p5[0].count}} students while boys account for {{p5[1].count}} students. 

Infrastructure gaps remain a concern, with {{p6[0].count}} schools lacking functional girls' toilets, {{p6[1].count}} lacking drinking water, and {{p6[2].count}} lacking electricity. 

The table highlights specific schools with multiple gaps, starting with {{p7}}.
